clues.title: Plate: black with white text
text: Tunisian licence plates are **black with white text**.
NOTE: Military plates feature a small Tunisian flag on the left side of the plate, which is visible on the dark green follow car.

images.caption: Tunisian plates: standard black and military, plus a pickup on the road

clues.summary: Plates are black with white writing. Military plates have a small flag on the left, visible on the dark green follow car.

clues.title: Google car: escorted by a follow car
text: One of the best ways to recognize Tunisia is that, in most coverage, the Google car is escorted by a **follow car**.
There are several different follow cars and these are four of the most commonly found ones.
NOTE: Follow cars can be in front of the street view car, or very far behind. Make sure to pan and zoom if you do not find them immediately.
clues.summary: In most coverage a second car follows the Google car, either right in front or far behind. Pan and zoom to find it. Several different follow cars exist.

clues.title: Google car: black with a thin medium antenna
text: The Google car in Tunisia is **black** with a medium-length, thin antenna.
NOTE: The colour of the car is not always perceptible. Make sure to look around for other more helpful clues.
clues.summary: A black car with a medium-length thin antenna. The car colour is not always clear, so look for other clues.

clues.title: Landscape: Mediterranean to semi-desert
text: Tunisia has Mediterranean, dry and semidesert climates.
NOTE: In the second step, you will find more about region specific climate and landscape.
clues.summary: The climate ranges from Mediterranean to dry and semi-desert, depending on the region.

clues.title: Plants: olive groves in neat rows
text: These **olive tree plantations** can often be found along roads. They consist of nicely arranged rows of olive trees on an often raked, weedless soil.
clues.summary: Olive tree plantations often line the roads, with trees in tidy rows over raked, weed-free soil.

clues.title: Road lines: white, edge lines dashed or solid
text: Tunisia usually has white road lines. Outer road lines can be dashed or solid.
NOTE: A few roads in Sfax have [yellow middle lines](https://goo.gl/maps/VWruqg6L6z9bPFxU6).
clues.summary: Road lines are usually white and edge lines can be dashed or solid. A few roads in the big southern coastal city have yellow middle lines.

clues.title: Language: French and Arabic
text: In Tunisia, both **French and Arabic** are common. The Arabic script can be identified by its lines and dots. You can often see [bilingual signs](https://goo.gl/maps/gS1SqVNEC2RM3KPq8).
NOTE: The UAE and (more rarely) Jordan use English and Arabic.
clues.summary: French and Arabic are both common, often on the same sign. Arabic script is recognised by its lines and dots. The UAE and, rarely, Jordan use English and Arabic instead.

differs.how: Uses English and Arabic, not French
Uses English and Arabic, not French

clues.title: Sign: white direction signs, Arabic and Latin
text: Most direction signs have a **white** background with towns listed in Arabic and Latin script. The font of the Latin script is usually quite distinctive.
NOTE: Many direction signs include the capital Tunis, but this does not necessarily mean you are anywhere near that city.
clues.summary: Direction signs mostly have a white background, with towns written in Arabic and Latin script in a distinctive font. The capital often appears even far from it.

clues.title: Houses: doors and gates in traditional blue
text: Doors, windows, gates and other architectural elements are sometimes painted with this specific traditional **shade of blue**.
NOTE: This shade of blue can be found all over the country, but is especially common on the island of Djerba, where buildings tend to be older and more traditional.
clues.summary: Doors, windows and gates are sometimes painted a particular traditional blue. It is found everywhere, but especially on the older island of Djerba.

clues.title: Curb: red and white stripes
text: **Red and white** striped curbs are common in Tunisia.
NOTE: Similar curbs are also common in Israel and Palestine. Make sure to look for additional information!

images.caption: Kerb painted in red and white stripes

clues.summary: Red and white striped curbs are common. Israel and Palestine have similar curbs, so check other clues.

clues.title: Route marker: white concrete post, coloured round top
text: These white concrete markers with a rounded top can be found throughout Tunisia. The top can be red, yellow or green.

NOTE: They are very useful for pinpointing your exact location. On either side, they show the distance in **kilometres to the nearest town**. The side facing the road shows the road number, in this case 1.
clues.summary: A white concrete marker with a rounded top that can be red, yellow or green. Each side shows the distance to the nearest town, and the road-facing side shows the road number.

clues.title: Sign: stop sign with Arabic and Latin text
text: Tunisia has a fairly unique **stop sign** with Arabic and Latin script.
NOTE: Similar stop signs can be found in Jordan and the UAE. However, Israel and Palestine use a different unique stop sign with a [hand](https://maps.app.goo.gl/cEbKb3viPzJEHuKS8) instead of text.
clues.summary: A stop sign with words in both Arabic and Latin script. Jordan and the UAE have similar ones. Israel and Palestine use a hand symbol instead of text.

differs.how: Uses a hand symbol instead of text

clues.title: Coverage: mostly the east coast
text: Coverage is mostly limited to the **east coast**, between Bizerte in the north and Medinine in the south. Most coverage is in bigger towns and on main roads. The biggest towns and the island of Djerba have quite extensive side road coverage.
clues.summary: Coverage is mostly on the east coast, from Bizerte in the north to Medenine in the south, in bigger towns and on main roads. The biggest towns and Djerba also have many side roads.

clues.title: Follow car: light green Toyota
text: This **light green Toyota** follow car can be found everywhere in the northernmost part of Tunisia. You will never see it south of Hammamet.

images.caption: Follow car: a light green Toyota

clues.summary: A light green Toyota follow car found in the far north. It is never seen south of Hammamet.

clues.title: Follow car: dark green Mazda, red-strip plate
text: The **dark green Mazda** is the most common follow car in Tunisia. This becomes apparent if you look at the coverage map, it can be found all the way from Hammamet to Djerba. Aside from the darker colour, it can also be recognized by its military licence plate with a **red strip** on the left.
clues.summary: The most common follow car, dark green, with a military plate that has a red strip on the left. It appears from Hammamet down to Djerba.

clues.title: Follow car: many different ones in the capital
text: Tunis, the capital of Tunisia, has **a lot of different follow cars**. Most of them can be found all over the city. The light green Toyota can also be spotted here.

images.caption: Follow cars: several different vehicles in the coverage

clues.summary: The capital has a lot of different follow cars all over the city. The light green Toyota can also appear.

clues.title: Follow car: white Mitsubishi, white mirrors
text: The city of Kairouan in central-northern Tunisia has this unique follow car, a **white Mitsubishi** with white mirrors. The dark green follow car can also sometimes be spotted following the Mitsubishi.
NOTE: Some white follow cars in Tunisia can look similar to the Kairouan car. However, none of them are Mitsubishis.

images.caption: Follow car: a white Mitsubishi with a white mirror

clues.summary: A white Mitsubishi with white mirrors in the central-northern city of Kairouan. The dark green follow car sometimes trails it. Other white follow cars exist but none are Mitsubishis.

clues.title: Coverage: usually no follow car on the island
text: The island of Djerba is the only region of Tunisia where you are usually **not** accompanied by a follow car. Most coverage completely lacks one.
While it is rare, this **white Mercedes** and the dark green follow car can be present.
clues.summary: Djerba is the one region usually without a follow car. Occasionally a white Mercedes or the dark green car appears.

clues.title: Landscape: hilly fallow farmland north of the capital
text: The area north of Tunis has a Mediterranean climate with hilly terrain. The region is very agricultural and at the time the coverage was captured, almost all fields laid fallow.
clues.summary: North of the capital is hilly Mediterranean farmland, with almost all fields lying fallow when photographed.

clues.title: Landscape: higher, greener hills on the east coast
text: The area between Tunis and Hammamet looks similar to the area north of Tunis, but the hills tend to be higher and more vegetated.
clues.summary: Between the capital and Hammamet looks like the area north of the capital, but with higher and more vegetated hills.

clues.title: Landscape: very flat, dry, olive groves
text: The large middle region between Hammamet and Gabes is very flat, and more arid. Olive tree plantations are common and the more south you go, the drier the landscape becomes.
clues.summary: The big middle region is very flat and dry. Olive groves are common and it gets drier further south.

clues.title: Landscape: desert-like, rubbish, small white rocks
text: South of Gabes is where the landscape changes into something more akin to a desert. A lot more rubbish and small white rocks can be found along the roads. Olive tree plantations are still somewhat common. A mountain range far in the distance is often visible to the southwest.
clues.summary: South of Gabes it turns desert-like, with more rubbish and small white rocks along the road. Olive groves are still fairly common, and a mountain range is often far to the south-west.

clues.title: Houses: whitewashed with blue doors, many palms
text: The island of Djerba can sometimes have a distinct vibe. There tend to be a lot of palm trees. Whitewashed, traditional buildings with blue doors and windows are common.
NOTE: Not all locations on the island will have this distinct vibe. A lack of a follow car is another good way to confirm that you are on Djerba.
clues.summary: Lots of palm trees and whitewashed traditional buildings with blue doors and windows. No follow car also confirms the island of Djerba.

clues.title: Landscape: teal lake with flat shores
text: Bizerte Lake is instantly recognizable due to its **teal coloured** waters**.** There are slight hills to its south, with the rest of the area around the lake being flat. The city of Bizerte is located on the northeast side of the lake.
clues.summary: A lake with teal-coloured water, slight hills to its south and flat land elsewhere around it. The city lies on its north-east side.

clues.title: Plants: lots of palms in one place
text: If you see **a large amount of palm trees** in a single place, you are probably in Gabes.
NOTE: While Djerba also has many palm trees, the towns and surrounding area tend to look more rural.
clues.summary: A big concentration of palm trees points to Gabes. Djerba has many palms too, but there the towns look more rural.

clues.title: Landscape: sandy hills in the flat south
text: On the P1 road northwest of Medinine, you can occasionally find sandy hills that look like this. These hills are quite unique, as most coverage in southern Tunisia is in very flat areas.
clues.summary: Occasional sandy hills on the main road north-west of Medenine. They stand out because most southern coverage is very flat.

clues.title: Road: dark offroad over bright sand, east-west
text: An offroad from road P12 southwest of Sousse can be recognised by the dark pavement surrounded by bright sandy soil combined with the east-west road angle. The eastern part of the road is fairly vegetated, with large numbers of prickly pears, while the western part of the road is [very arid](https://maps.app.goo.gl/W7Q3a5DgLqsJuio59) with little to no vegetation.
clues.summary: A dark paved track through bright sandy soil running east-west. The east end has many prickly pears; the west end is very dry and barren.

clues.title: Road: causeway with water on both sides, pipeline
text: You can easily recognise the Djerba-Zarzis causeway thanks to the **water on both sides** and the **pipeline** that is always present to your west.

images.caption: A causeway with water on both sides

clues.summary: A causeway with water on both sides and a pipeline always on your west. It joins the island of Djerba to the mainland.

clues.title: Coverage: walking backpack at sights nationwide
text: Trekkers can be found all over the country, even in places far away from the area with car coverage. Coverage includes [archaeological sites](https://goo.gl/maps/2UsBo8HPFhKwi1rs5), [forts](https://goo.gl/maps/UQP4Wuk1jgp4F58v5), [mosques](https://goo.gl/maps/xaFQEbu3Nq5kQ5Q37), and a [Star Wars set](https://goo.gl/maps/y36NttMDLurqthHu5), among other things.
clues.summary: Walking-backpack coverage appears all over the country, even far from car coverage. It includes archaeological sites, forts, mosques and a Star Wars film set.
